---
title: "🧪 Small example"
aliases:
  - tutorial.html
---

This example is deliberately small, and its parameter values are not meant to be realistic. It follows just 3 human hosts (`--Nh`) for 10 generations (`--T`), with 2 parasites passed on per mosquito bite (`--K`), a superinfection probability of 0.18 (`--chi`) and 1 oocyst per mosquito (`--C`). Keeping the simulation this small makes it quick to run and easy to read: you can see each human host and each generation clearly, and follow exactly how parasites are transmitted between hosts, where superinfection brings strains together, and where mutations arise along the way. Use it to get a feel for how the model works before moving on to the [realistic example](tutorial-realistic.qmd), which uses more realistic values.

## Run the notebook

The Jupyter notebook runs every `krsim` command on this example and looks at what each one writes. Change the parameters to see how transmission changes. With the `krsim` environment active ([Installation](installation.qmd)), run the commands below. The first saves the notebook into your current folder and the second opens it in Jupyter:

```bash
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrc-ide/KR_simulator/main/notebooks/tutorial.ipynb
jupyter notebook tutorial.ipynb
```

The notebook writes its files to `output/` next to it.

::: {.column-screen-inset-right}
## Visualise transmission

The notebook also draws two interactive maps of the true pedigree. These are the maps from this example (seed 123); both are interactive, so you can try them here.

**Pairwise strain pedigree map.** Pick two current strains and trace each one's ancestry back through the pedigree. Where the two lineages meet are their shared ancestors. [Open full screen](maps/pairwise_strain_pedigree_map_123.html){target="_blank"}

<iframe class="fit-height" src="maps/pairwise_strain_pedigree_map_123.html" width="100%" height="850" style="border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 4px;"></iframe>

**Strain transmission and mutation map.** Who infected whom, generation by generation: founders at the top, current strains at the bottom, one lane per host. Each × is a mutation, drawn on the link and at the time it happened. Pick a chromosome, then a tree in the bar, to see just the genealogy of that stretch of genome and its mutations; click a strain to highlight its ancestors and descendants. [Open full screen](maps/strain_transmission_map_123.html){target="_blank"}

<iframe class="fit-height" src="maps/strain_transmission_map_123.html" width="100%" height="850" style="border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 4px;"></iframe>
:::

```{=html}
<script>
// Grow each embedded map to fit its content, so the whole transmission chain
// shows without an inner scrollbar. Measure the map's content (.wrap), not the
// page: the map page stretches to the frame's height, which would feed back.
document.querySelectorAll("iframe.fit-height").forEach(frame => {
  const fit = () => {
    try {
      const wrap = frame.contentDocument.querySelector(".wrap");
      frame.style.height = Math.ceil(wrap.getBoundingClientRect().bottom + 40) + "px";
    } catch (e) {}
  };
  frame.addEventListener("load", () => {
    fit();
    try { new ResizeObserver(fit).observe(frame.contentDocument.querySelector(".wrap")); } catch (e) {}
  });
});
</script>
```
